narrative.text:
Upstream main is `ca8f6b1193154384e4626921255f86923fc5edf3`; PR #12’s head is still `21a7ebcb38ab901c2e721b325c63fe8407ae7a7a`.

I’ve read both reviews, all inline comments, and the discussion. The only textual merge conflict is `test/harness.ts`. I’ll isolate typing in `slack.typing`, retain messaging without that grant, and use the review’s conservative top-level option: no status where publish would reply outside a thread. The remaining fixes cover accepted/addressed-message tracking, refusal suppression, lifecycle cleanup, serialized calls, tests, and stale documentation. I’m recording Step 0 before editing source.The regression suite is green: it fails 15 of 20 tests against #12’s mechanically ported approach, then passes after the fixes. A separate mutation of the 60-second refresh boundary also fails as expected.

Both upstream baselines passed: 584/584 on Node 22.23.3 and 24.22.1. The first full implementation run exposed test doubles missing the new cleanup methods and a handshake assertion that assumed every feature was granted. I’ve updated those test fixtures while keeping the shared harness grant unchanged—without typing.Committed locally as `be7c3af18f95ae14e01dc917a145381ea5fa5896`, directly on upstream `ca8f6b1`.

All final gates passed: 607/607 tests on both Node versions (baseline 584/584), 117/117 touched tests on Node 22.12.0, plus installs, typechecks, builds, release dry fold, and changelog checks. The report includes Step 0, review dispositions, red/green evidence, draft replies, and residual risks. Nothing was pushed or posted.
